note: S75 runs W2/S74 declared falsifier against elders/PathMap 0.3.0. Fires on variable-length atom keys, does not on fixed-length triple keys. pathmap merkleize is dedup, not a commitment.

controls.name: C_identical_key_sets
controls.must_fire_because: pathmap and the Python trie disagree on how many keys they loaded -- the comparison would be between different inputs
controls.can_fail_because: either pathmap keys count differs from the dumped count
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

controls.name: C_probe_reads_pathmap_correctly
controls.must_fire_because: pathmap's own 8-path test set does not give 6 nodes through this probe -- then the probe is misreading the library and the verdict is VOID, not negative
controls.can_fail_because: the tiny set reports any node count other than 6
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

controls.name: C_falsifier_fires_on_atoms
controls.must_fire_because: the mean node-depth ratio on atom keys is under 10.0x -- the falsifier would NOT fire and S73/S74's proof sizes would transfer to real pathmap
controls.can_fail_because: depth_ratio_mean for atoms reads below the threshold
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

controls.name: C_falsifier_does_not_fire_on_triples
controls.must_fire_because: fixed-length triple keys ALSO exceed the threshold -- then the cause is not key length and the mechanism claimed here is wrong
controls.can_fail_because: depth_ratio_mean for triples reads above the threshold
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

controls.name: C_merkleize_is_deterministic
controls.must_fire_because: pathmap's merkleize hash changes between two runs on the same trie -- it would not be content-derived
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

controls.name: C_merkleize_is_dedup_not_commitment
controls.must_fire_because: pathmap depends on any cryptographic hash -- then it can emit a real commitment and W2 may have reimplemented something that existed
controls.can_fail_because: a sha2/sha3/blake3/keccak/digest dependency appears in pathmap Cargo.toml
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

observations.hash_is_gxhash_declared_for: for dag_serialization, merkleization, and caching catamorphism
observations.name_grep_was_a_false_positive: fn witness in pathmap is a Rust borrow token (-> Self::WitnessT, several -> ()), not a proof

controls.name: C_dedup_actually_reuses
controls.must_fire_because: merkleize reuses no nodes on either corpus -- the structural sharing S73's cost model leans on would be absent here
controls.can_fail_because: reused reads 0 for atoms or for triples
controls.null_must_contain: the opposite depth ratio, or a pathmap proof function

falsifier: Show that authentication path length does NOT scale with node depth on pathmap -- e.g. a proof scheme over it whose size is independent of the number of nodes on the path. That would restore S73/S74 proof sizes on variable-length keys.
